content_blocks.label: lead_paragraph
content_blocks.text: Congressman Thomas Johnson has introduced sweeping gun control legislation that would ban most semi-automatic weapons and require universal background checks at gun shows, drawing immediate backlash from conservative groups.

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_1
content_blocks.text: Johnson's bill, titled the 'Public Safety Act,' aims to reduce gun violence through stricter regulations, but critics argue it infringes on Second Amendment rights and will do little to prevent mass shootings.

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_2
content_blocks.text: In a statement, Johnson said, 'We need to protect our communities from the senseless tragedies that occur every day due to unchecked access to firearms.'

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_3
content_blocks.text: Rep. Sarah Lee, a Republican colleague, called the proposal 'unconstitutional nonsense' and vowed to fight its passage in Congress.

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_4
content_blocks.text: The bill has garnered support from numerous advocacy groups focused on reducing gun-related deaths, while opposition has come from pro-gun organizations who see the legislation as a threat to their members' freedoms.

content_blocks.label: pull_quote
content_blocks.text: ‘This isn’t about safety; this is about stripping away our rights.’ - Rep. Sarah Lee
